programs.title: The Flood 1: First Pulse
programs.desc: The Okavango Delta is a water phenomenon on the sands of the Kalahari Desert.Every year, heavy rains transform the barren region into a true oasis teeming with life.In a two-part documentary, director Brad Bestelink introduced the inhabitants of this unique place on Earth.The camera lens included both small dragonflies and giant elephants.Spectacular photos were taken from various perspectives - from the ground, from a bird's eye view and from the water depths.Scenes of exciting hunting intertwine with the idyll of life in a fertile land.Masters of survival The story begins while waiting for rain.On a sun-baked, dry and barren land, there is a fight for survival.Wild cats - a cheetah and a leopard - show off their skills.She stands out for her speed, he is able to lure his prey into an ambush.They both turn out to be effective in hunting, for example, impala.As the rain pours down, the region undergoes an almost magical transformation.The water attracts herds of various animals.Among them are African buffalos, which are hunted by lions.Viewers will also learn about the adventures of a longclaw who tries alone to ensure the safety of three chicks.Scenes from the lives of various species form a story about a complex ecosystem.
